messages:
maya: Heads up — we got pager alerts for org 8732 being throttled but metering shows they’re under their monthly quota. Enforcement returned 429s for ~2m window. Anyone seen this pattern before?

leo: Yep saw a spike ~10:15 UTC. Enforcement consumer lag on the metering topic jumped. Likely read-side lag = stale counts -> false throttles.

sarah: Confirmed, looking at the enforcement pod logs. Consumer offset behind by ~180k msgs, commit heartbeat delays.

rahul: To add context: enforcement checkpoints offsets every 30s and applies a sliding-window evaluation at commit time. If Kafka lag > window, enforcement makes decisions on last-committed state which can be minutes old during bursts.

maya: Right — that matches. We have two problems: (1) metering pipeline lag under burst => enforcement sees old low counts and MAY under-throttle (but here it over-throttled?) and (2) enforcement is also using an aggregated view that can overcount when duplicate events land during retry/backpressure.

leo: In this incident it looks like enforcement accidentally double-applied some delta because the reconciler backfill job re-emitted events after a transient failure. So enforcement bumped local counters and then later replayed same deltas.

metering-bot: [automated] producer-latency-spike detected on topic redwood.metering.events at 2026-03-02T10:14:22Z. Producer retry count increased x6.

rahul: Quick diagnostic commands I ran:
```
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server pk1:9092 --describe --group enforcement-consumer
# shows lag: 182,430 messages, last-lag-timestamp ~2026-03-02T10:13:00Z
```

leo: Possible remediation options: reduce checkpoint interval to 5s, or move to a local proxy token-bucket that enforces soft-limits instantly and relies on eventual reconciliation to correct counts. Tradeoffs: local proxy prevents false 429s but can allow temporary overuse.

sarah: We should also add a short circuit: if consumer lag > threshold (say 30s/100k msgs) flip enforcement to 'grace' mode for that org (serve at slow/soft rate) and surface in the console. Safer than blind allow.

maya: Agree. Proposal: implement a 3-part fix: 1) short term: lower commit interval + guard against replayed deltas (idempotency by event_id), 2) medium term: implement proxy-side leaky-bucket with local credit and soft-fail behavior when backlog detected, 3) long term: add real-time stream route (gRPC/redis-stream) from API gateway -> enforcement for per-key counters.

leo: For (1), reducing commit interval likely cheap. But idempotency requires event_id persisted (we have that in the payload but enforcement store currently doesn't dedupe). I can push a tiny migration to store last_event_id per key.

rahul: Note: storing last_event_id at per-token granularity could be heavy. Instead store a short LRU cache in enforcement for recent event IDs + a tombstone TTL of 10m. That should avoid most replays without big DB churn.

sarah: I'll wire up a dashboard panel (console -> Quota enforcement) that shows consumer_lag, replay_rate, and org_fallback_state per org. Also add an alert when enforcement flips to grace for >1min.

billing-bot: [automated] org 8732: grace_mode enabled at 2026-03-02T10:17:05Z by eng-platform (incident auto-detect).

maya: Action items: leo -> reduce commit interval + event dedupe prototype. rahul -> design LRU cache pattern and estimate memory. sarah -> add dashboard + alert. I'll open the ticket and coordinate a canary.

leo: quick patch I'll ship tonight: reduce checkpoint to 5s, add metric enforcement.commit_interval_seconds, and a log line when dedupe triggers. Canary 2 pods in prod region a.

rahul: I'll prepare a short doc for proxy-side token-bucket behavior: soft vs hard limits, how to refund after reconciliation, and abuse-detection heuristics.

maya: Good. Also we should add a console UX note: show 'quota state freshness' under Quotas so customers understand when enforcement is working off potentially stale metrics.

leo: +1 — that will cut down on support tickets.

sarah: Pushed dashboard draft to staging. panel id: enforcement_health. I'll drop link in #eng-monitoring after review.

maya: Thanks. I'll create the tracking item: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-1864 and assign. Can we aim for stabilizing the checkpoint/dedupe in the next 48h?

leo: Yep. I'll open the PR soon.

rahul: FYI: we should also run a one-off backfill reconciliation that reviews delta-applications for last 24h and credit any orgs that were overcharged due to replays. I'll coordinate with billing.

billing-bot: [automated] created ticket BILL-492: backfill reconciliation requested for 2026-03-02 incident.

maya: Great. If anyone sees more orgs affected, ping here. Otherwise we proceed with the plan. :thumbsup:

leo: I'll post progress updates in this thread.

sarah: Thanks all.
